record.original_question: Consider a general nonnormal matrix $A = V Lambda V^-1$ with largest eigenvalue magnitude $lambda_1$ and finite eigenvector condition number $kappa_V = |V | |V^-1 |$. Is there an algorithm that uses $ ( (nkappa_V),1/epsilon)$ matrix-vector products with $A$ and returns $lambda$ so that $|lambda - lambda'| epsilon |lambda_1|$, where $lambda'$ is any eigenvalue of $A$ with $|lambda' | (1-epsilon) lambda_1$?

evidence.quote: Consider a general nonnormal matrix $A = V \Lambda V^{-1}$ with largest eigenvalue magnitude $\lambda_1$ and finite eigenvector condition number $\kappa_V = \|V\| \|V^{-1}\|$. Is there an algorithm that uses $\poly(\log(n\kappa_V),1/\epsilon)$ matrix-vector products with $A$ and returns $\lambda$ so that $|\lambda - \lambda'| \le \epsilon |\lambda_1|$, where $\lambda'$ is any eigenvalue of $A$ with $|\lambda' | \ge (1-\epsilon)\abs{\lambda_1}$?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ be a (possibly nonnormal) diagonalizable matrix written as $A = V \Lambda V^{-1}$, where $\Lambda = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)$ with $|\lambda_1| \ge |\lambda_2| \ge \cdots \ge |\lambda_n|$, and let the eigenvector condition number be $\kappa_V = \|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|<\infty$ (operator $2$-norm). One is allowed only "matrix-vector product" queries to $A$: in each query, an algorithm chooses a (possibly randomized, possibly adaptive) vector $v \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and receives $Av$.

Given $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, decide whether there exists an algorithm that, using at most
$$\mathrm{poly}\!\left(\log(n\kappa_V),\, 1/\epsilon\right)$$
matrix-vector product queries to $A$, outputs a complex number $\widehat\lambda$ such that
$$|\widehat\lambda - \lambda'| \le \epsilon\,|\lambda_1|$$
for some eigenvalue $\lambda'$ of $A$ satisfying $|\lambda'| \ge (1-\epsilon)\,|\lambda_1|$. Either exhibit such an algorithm or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.category_tag: Matrix-vector query complexity for eigenvalue approximation
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. The problem of approximating the top eigenvalue of a general nonnormal diagonalizable matrix in poly(log(n κ_V), 1/ε) matrix-vector queries appears to remain an open question in the matrix-vector query complexity literature; results are known for normal/Hermitian cases (e.g., via Lanczos/Krylov methods), but the nonnormal regime with dependence only polylog in κ_V is not known to be settled.

status_evidence.title: Power iteration - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Standard power/Krylov methods are analyzed for normal or symmetric matrices; convergence for general nonnormal matrices depends on eigenvector conditioning.
status_evidence.claim: No general matrix-vector query algorithm with polylog(n κ_V) complexity is documented in standard references.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvalue algorithm - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Existing eigenvalue algorithms for nonnormal matrices typically have polynomial dependence on dimension or condition number, not merely polylogarithmic.
status_evidence.claim: The polylog(n κ_V) matrix-vector complexity for nonnormal top-eigenvalue approximation is not established in the standard literature.
